title: Learning Platform Operations & Migration Readiness
summary: I supported a large LMS migration and launch by testing employee, partner, and customer experiences; validating content, learning plans, certifications, renewals, visibility, and navigation; documenting issues; and supporting launch readiness.

content.business_need: Move learning into a new LMS without losing learner history, certification logic, learning-path relationships, audience visibility, or a usable learner experience.
content.audience: Employees, partners, customers, and the learning stakeholders who supported the platform transition.
learning_objectives: Validate learner-facing catalogs, learning plans, certifications, renewal paths, navigation, and content before launch.
Test employee, partner, and customer experiences from a learner point of view.
Identify content mapping, duplicate-content, visibility, and relationship issues before they reached learners.
Document issues, support triage, and contribute to launch-readiness and learner-support work.
content.role: Instructional designer and LMS content administrator supporting migration, UAT, content validation, and launch.
content.design_approach: I treated the migration as both a platform change and a learner-experience change. I tested what learners could see and do, checked the structures behind those journeys, documented issues, and worked with the broader migration team to resolve problems before and after launch.
content.development_process: Participated in UAT for employee, partner, and customer experiences; validated catalogs, learning plans, certifications, renewals, thumbnails, navigation, and learner-facing content; surfaced mapping, duplicate-content, and visibility issues; reviewed learner guidance; and supported issue triage and launch readiness.
outcomes: Directly supported LMS migration testing, content validation, learning-plan reviews, learner-experience audits, certification workflow testing, and launch support.
Helped surface content mapping, duplicate-content, and visibility issues before launch.
Contributed reusable UAT, content-validation, certification-review, learner-support, governance, and migration-readiness practices.

detail_sections.title: Test the parts learners actually touch.
detail_sections.summary: I checked learner-facing behavior and the platform structures behind it before launch.

items.title: Audience visibility
items.body: Tested employee, partner, and customer experiences and checked whether content appeared to the right audiences.

items.title: Learning plans
items.body: Reviewed learning-plan structure, relationships, and learner-facing behavior in the new platform.

items.title: Certifications + renewals
items.body: Tested certification workflows and reviewed renewal paths so repeat learners followed the intended experience.

items.title: Content + navigation
items.body: Validated learner-facing content, thumbnails, navigation, catalogs, and supporting materials for launch readiness.

items.title: Issue triage
items.body: Documented problems, supported troubleshooting, and helped move launch-readiness issues toward resolution.

detail_sections.title: Catch problems before they become learner problems.
detail_sections.summary: The migration created new structures and relationships that needed active validation.
rows: Whether migrated content was connected to the intended learning structure.
Incorrect mapping could break the learner journey or completion logic.
Overlapping or repeated records created during transition work.
Duplicates could confuse learners and administrators.
Which audiences could see catalogs, training, and learning structures.
The right content had to appear to the right learner group.
How certification and renewal paths behaved for returning learners.
Renewal logic needed to preserve a clear repeat-learning experience.
Navigation, onboarding guidance, and support resources.
A technically correct migration still needed to be understandable to learners.
detail_sections.note: This is a public-safe reconstruction. Internal configuration, learner records, issue logs, and proprietary screenshots are omitted.

detail_sections.title: My contribution moved from testing into launch support.
detail_sections.summary: I worked inside the broader migration effort rather than owning the entire platform transition.

items.title: Onboarding guidance

detail_sections.title: Keep the contribution accurate.
detail_sections.summary: This case shows the migration work I directly supported without claiming ownership of the full platform program.

items.title: Directly supported
items.body: UAT, content validation, learning-plan reviews, learner-experience audits, certification workflow testing, issue triage, and launch support.

items.title: Reusable work
items.body: UAT processes, validation approaches, learner-support patterns, certification-review workflows, governance practices, and readiness checklists.

items.title: Not claimed
items.body: I do not claim ownership of the full migration, platform architecture, or quantitative business impact.

detail_sections.title: What the migration reinforced for me.
detail_sections.summary: LMS migrations depend on governance, testing, and learner communication as much as configuration.

items.title: Test by role
items.body: Employee, partner, and customer experiences need to be tested as different learner journeys rather than assumed to behave the same way.

items.title: Validate before launch
items.body: Early UAT and content validation make mapping, visibility, renewal, and navigation problems easier to catch before they spread.

items.title: Treat support as part of launch
items.body: Learner guidance and support resources matter because a technically correct platform change can still be confusing to use.
